Stonebeck climbs toward convergence as public marks lead the way

RATING: overweight

Stonebeck's private book enters 2028-03-15 carrying a reported_vs_public_gap of -8.5%, and we read this gap through our structural prior: growth and policy support resolve stress over time, and marks tend to catch up to fundamentals rather than the reverse. The newsflow that "public rally leaves private marks behind" is not, in our view, evidence of hidden fragility—it is the ordinary lag of private valuation processes behind faster-moving public comparables. When "listed comps rerate sharply," private marks historically follow with a delay, not a divergence that compounds indefinitely.

The macro backdrop supports this reading. cpi_now at 2.7% sits close enough to target ranges that the policy_rate_now of 4.75% has room to ease over the coming cycle, and hy_spread_now_bps at 380bps remains well inside levels associated with systemic stress. Drawdown of +0.0% confirms that, whatever the reported-versus-public gap implies about marks, realized losses have not materialized. We view this as consistent with our house prior: policy support and steady growth give private assets time to reprice upward rather than default downward.

Where some observers see "fragilities compounding beneath stable marks," we see marks that have simply not yet been refreshed to reflect a rally that has already lifted comparable public names. The one_year_return of +9.3% suggests the asset class has room to compound further once private marks close the gap, even as ytd_return of +1.0% shows the catch-up has only begun.

The risk to our view: should the reported_vs_public_gap persist or widen rather than close, it could signal that private marks are lagging for structural reasons—illiquidity, stale appraisal cycles—rather than simply catching up, and we would need to revisit our overweight. We believe convergence is the more likely path, but prudent investors should watch the gap closely over coming quarters before adding further exposure.
